NRL Late Mail: Round 26 - Cleary set to debut
Halfback Jett Cleary will make his debut alongside Luke Hanson after the Warriors chose to rest Te Maire Martin and Chanel Harris-Tavita.
Martin was named on Tuesday to return from a hamstring complaint which kept him out of the last three matches against Penrith, Brisbane and South Sydney.
However, he has been omitted as has Harris-Tavita who has a minor hamstring issue. Both will train fully next week to line up in the final regular season match against the Sea Eagles.
Roosters skipper James Tedesco will again look to make his comeback from an ankle injury after being named to face the Dolphins.
Tedesco suffered the injury in Round 22 against the Cowboys and has struggled to get it right across the past fortnight, twice being named to play before being a late withdrawal.

The Roosters’ recent winning streak had them looking the goods for the minor premiership, but a second upset loss to the Tigers in consecutive seasons last weekend saw them lose ground for top spot to the Warriors. They sit third only on points difference to the Warriors and Penrith, but such is the competitiveness in the top teams this season that a loss to the Dolphins of 12 points or more could see this week’s opponents overtake them and keep alive the slenderest of minor premiership hopes.
One does wonder if the timing of the Tigers’ loss last weekend will be a good or bad thing for the Dolphins. Was it the beginning of a late-season wobble, or just a blip that the Dolphins will get punished for this weekend? The eight-game winning run before last weekend’s loss suggests it’s a blip, but it’s interesting to note in that eight-game run the average winning margin was only eight points, if you exclude the 72-point lesson they handed the Cowboys. Against a stinging Roosters side looking to also make amends for the 48-10 loss they suffered last time these two sides met in Round 15, they can ill afford to give up such a head start.

items.body_excerpt:
Life of Brian: Dolphins rookie Pouniu ready to ride the wave
Dolphins rookie Brian Pouniu announced himself as a player of the future with his breakout performance in the win over the Eels, looking more than comfortable in just his second NRL game.
A ‘late’ promotion to start in the second row in place of the injured Connelly Lemuelu, the Auckland-born talent topped the Dolphins' tackle count with 39 and also made the most metres for a forward (179).
Brian Pouniu makes a run for the Dolphins. ©Zain Mohammed / NRL Images
Still only 18 years old, after making his NRL debut back in Round 12 at centre in the win over the Raiders, Pouniu has spent most of this season developing his game with the Redcliffe Dolphins in Queensland’s Hostplus Cup.
He also made a cameo for the NRL Dolphins NRLQ Under 21 side in their Round 11 win over the Titans.
For the club, there is even more reason to celebrate his progress as Pouniu becomes the first player to come through and play at every level of their academy.
“(I felt) really good (playing in the second row) … it was actually Max Plath that was meant to come as a starter, but Woolfy [coach Kristian Woolf] trusted my ability to start and then play the full 80, so I'm just grateful," Pouniu said.
“He had a plan straight after Connolly got injured, he said I'll play the next week, and then he just said you'll start …
“I guess being at a young age (I am) extremely grateful the coaches trusted me with the job...
'He's got great football IQ': Pouniu embracing new Titans role
“I'm just really grateful for this club … playing my first Cup game this year and then playing my first NRL game this year.
"I think the jump is pretty major from Cup to NRL, but it was a good experience from coming from Cup to NRL.”
Pouniu’s rise top the grade has plenty of extra meaning for the youngster. He is also living the dream of his older brother Joseph, who was also a talented forward before suffering a serious spinal cord injury during a game that cut short his promising rugby league career.
Now working as an analyst with the Gold Coast Titans, the club where he was signed as a player, the younger Pouniu was still taking advice from his big brother.
“If you know me, obviously know my brother,” Pouniu said.
“I'm certain he would have played NRL if he was still playing and I carry him on my back every time I play.
“He is (still involved in rugby league); extremely grateful for the Titans for giving him the opportunity to still work there after everything.
“He still loves his footy, so I'm glad.
“(He still gives me advice) 100 percent.
“He cut some videos up for me, so it's good.”
Brian Pouniu embraces with Daine Laurie after making his NRL debut in Canberra in Round 12. ©NRL Images
With Redcliffe sitting in second spot on the Cup ladder, Pouniu will be playing finals football either way later this season and was making sure he would be ready to perform if given another opportunity to feature in the NRL.
Taking on tips from some of the most experienced players in the NRL squad, including Lemuelu, Pouniu was excited to see what was coming next.
“I'm just worrying about my own job," Pouniu said.
“Whenever someone gets injured, it's next man up mentality, so I just try to play for the boys.
“(I look up to) heaps of the older boys, Fus [Felise Kaufusi], Connolly Lemuelu, Kodi Nikorima and Herbie Farnworth.
“Having them on the left edge makes my job more easier.
“We'll see what the next few weeks hold for me, but I will do anything that the coach asks of me … but basically the first job is finals.
“If someone in the backrow gets injured, then I'll put my hand up for that job.”
The Dolphins will next take on the Roosters in a battle between third and fourth on Saturday.

Match Preview: Round 26 – Dolphins v Roosters
The finals are locked in, but there is still plenty on the line when the Dolphins head to Sydney for a top-four showdown with the Roosters.
Third meets fourth in Round 26, giving the Dolphins another opportunity to test themselves against one of the competition’s leading sides as September approaches.
The Dolphins arrive in Sydney with momentum after their victory over the Eels last Friday night, while the Roosters will be looking to respond following a loss to the Tigers.
The two sides last met during the Origin period in Round 15, when the Dolphins produced a dominant 48-10 victory at Suncorp Stadium.
This time, the challenge comes in Sydney and with both sides preparing for finals football.
The Dolphins will take confidence from their record on the road, having won all three games they have played in Sydney this season.
Jamayne Isaako also enters the clash on the verge of another club record. The winger needs five points to surpass his own Dolphins record for most points in a season, having set the benchmark with 278 points in 2025.
Isaako is also within reach of rare territory, sitting 26 points away from becoming just the fourth player to score 300 points in an NRL season.
Team News
Dolphins
Kristian Woolf has backed the side that secured victory over the Eels last Friday night, naming an unchanged 17 to face the Roosters.
Max Plath returns to the back row after a late change to the final team last Friday saw Brian Pouniu elevated into the starting side.
Pouniu remains in the 17 for his third NRL appearance after an impressive 80-minute performance against the Eels.
Roosters
James Tedesco has again been named to return from the ankle injury that has sidelined him for three games, with Cody Ramsey moving to the bench.
Nat Butcher starts at lock in place of Victor Radley, who is unavailable following a head knock, while Taylor Losalu joins the interchange.
Match-Up
Jack Bostock v Robert Toia
Two of Origin’s emerging centres will go head-to-head in a match-up that could have a major say in the contest.
Robert Toia has been a constant threat for the Roosters this season, scoring 11 tries and providing 12 try assists across 19 appearances. He has also recorded 89 tackle breaks and 12 line breaks while averaging 111 running metres per game.
Jack Bostock has been just as influential for the Dolphins. Across 12 appearances, he has scored five tries and produced 11 try assists, along with 28 tackle breaks and five line breaks. His work with the ball has also been a feature, averaging 162 running metres per game.
With both centres capable of creating opportunities on their respective edges, their defence will need to be on point. Limiting each other's time and space could be crucial as Bostock and Toia go head-to-head in Sydney.

items.body_excerpt:
Nothing to fear here: Dolphins up for finals audition
As the Dolphins approach their first finals campaign, experienced campaigners Felise Kaufusi and Morgan Knowles know what to expect and can't wait for the challenge.
Inaugural signing and club leader Kaufusi has won two premierships with the Storm, while Knowles boasts four titles with St Helens - both view the Round 26 match-up with the Roosters as the ideal September audition.
“I think it's come at a good time of year,” Kaufusi said.
“We're coming up against the No.3 team, the Sydney Roosters and I'm sure they'll be up for a big one, especially after last week's performance.
“It's a good little audition I think for us for times to come.
Related Match Preview
Roosters v Dolphins: Teddy set to play; Donoghoe good to go
“I think it's pretty exciting (to be heading into finals soon), it's uncharted waters for us as a club to be playing the finals, so it’s an exciting time.
“We've played some good footy (during the) last month and I still think you've got to take it week by week.
“We've still got two more regular season games before the new competition kicks off, so all our focus is on this week.”
Morgan Knowles with the ball for the Dolphins. ©Anthony Kourembanas / NRL Images
For Englishman Knowles, who has a remarkable strike rate of never missing finals in 12 years of playing in Super League and NRL, the Roosters provide the ideal test of their credentials.
"We've probably known for a couple of weeks that we're going to be in the finals and it's obviously new for the club and the group," Knowles said.
"It's exciting and we're obviously looking ahead to this week first and then Gold Coast, but we're really looking forward to what's to come and trying to peak at the right time.
"We are just looking for a good performance this week against the Roosters, a top team that are there in the four with us as well, so we'll be looking for a good performance.
"It's not the be all and end all (if we don't win), but we're looking for good performance and hopefully get the result.
"It's clear to see, just looking at the Roosters' team sheet, how many good players they've got right across the park, so it's not a case of circling out of any one individual or anything.
"They're a great team and that's why they've won lot of to competitions, so we have to be really good this weekend."

August 27 th 2026, 10:12am , By: Ben Bridge
Saturday evening at Allianz Stadium delivers the game of the round, and potentially one of the most important matches of the entire regular season. The Roosters sit third, the Dolphins fourth, and the winner puts itself in prime position for a top 2 finish if either the Warriors or Panthers slip over the final fortnight.
Ben Bridge is back with his preview and NRL tips for the Roosters vs Dolphins !

The stakes could hardly be higher, and that is exactly why I prefer a margin market rather than trying to force a side. Either side to win by 1-12 points is the best betting angle in a contest I expect to remain tight deep into the second half.
The Roosters are coming off the upset of the season, somehow losing 25-24 to the Tigers after entering as enormous favourites. The Dolphins, meanwhile, overcame a slow start to beat Parramatta 34-16 and remain firmly inside the top four.
James Tedesco has again been named to return after three games out with an ankle injury, although his status remains one to monitor. Victor Radley is out after a head knock, with Nat Butcher starting at lock. The Dolphins are virtually unchanged from last week and have Max Plath back in the starting side.
Roosters Cop Massive Reality Check
The Roosters’ 25-24 loss to Wests Tigers was an extraordinary result and a reminder that no team can afford to coast at this stage of the season. Sydney had an opportunity to consolidate top spot and instead became victims of one of the biggest upsets of 2026, with Jock Madden kicking the winning field goal in the 79th minute.
The decisive moment came after Naufahu Whyte attempted a loose offload while the Roosters were attacking. Terrell May intercepted, Wests moved into position and Madden calmly slotted the field goal from around 30 metres out.
It was a costly defeat. The Chooks dropped from first to third and now have almost no margin for error in the race for a top 2 finish. That makes this week fascinating.
The Roosters have been one of the competition’s best teams across the second half of the season, and one poor result does not erase that. Daly Cherry-Evans and Sam Walker remain one of the best halves combinations in the competition, Reece Robson has added enormous control at hooker and their forward pack can match almost anyone.
Tedesco’s possible return would be massive. He has been named several times recently without ultimately taking the field, so his status needs watching, but if he plays, he restores the home team’s best yardage player and support runner.
Radley’s absence takes away some middle aggression and defensive leadership, but Nat Butcher is a reliable replacement.
Most importantly, there should be absolutely no complacency this week. The Tigers loss was the warning shot. Against a Dolphins side capable of putting 40 on anyone, the Roosters will know another slow performance could cost them a home final.
Dolphins Clinch Their Opportunity
The Dolphins’ 34-16 victory over Parramatta was another example of their ability to recover after a poor start. The Eels raced to a 10-0 lead, but the Dolphins eventually overwhelmed them with their back five power and superior middle depth.
Herbie Farnworth and Selwyn Cobbo were enormous, combining for 480 run metres from 39 carries and 16 tackle breaks, while Jamayne Isaako added two tries and five goals. items.title: Joey’s major concern for Roosters in ‘make or break’ clash - Nine.com.au
items.snippet: Joey’s major concern for Roosters in ‘make or break’ clash    Nine.com.au
items.body_excerpt:
Andrew Johns has raised question marks over the Sydney Roosters ′ premiership credentials ahead of their “make or break” clash with the Dolphins .
After climbing to the top of the NRL ladder a fortnight ago with a gritty win over Penrith , things have unravelled slightly for the boys from Bondi.
Roosters halfback Sam Walker. Getty Images
In one of the biggest upsets of the year, the Roosters went down 25-24 to the struggling Wests Tigers , which saw them slide to third on the table.
Trent Robinson ’s men face an incredibly tough final two games of the regular season, first against the dangerous Dolphins before a round 27 showdown with local rivals South Sydney, who are expected to have Latrell Mitchell back.
Speaking on Wide World of Sports’ Immortal Behaviour to preview the Saturday evening blockbuster, Johns conceded that a loss to the Dolphins could result in the Roosters dropping out of the top-four and dashing their title hopes.
“It’s make or break for both, it’s so important for both these teams and I think more for the Roosters,” the rugby league Immortal said.
“I wouldn’t say it’s their biggest game of the year, but it’s the one with the biggest implications. They don’t wanna lose going into the last round against Souths.
Read more
‘A big thing’: Bennett reveals how ‘special’ Arrow plan was hatched
“If the Roosters lose [to the Dolphins], they can drop out of the four. This game has got huge implications, and you can’t win outside the top four, no team has done it and there’s a reason for that because it’s too hard.
“You look at that game against the Panthers and do you say it took it out of them? We’re gonna see where they’re at this weekend. If they lose, wow - it puts so much pressure on them going into that game against South Sydney.
“If the Roosters lose, I think they’ll miss the top four.”
As it stands, the Roosters are on 38 competition points – one win ahead of the Dolphins and two wins ahead of Cronulla – but two losses in the final two weeks would likely see them slip to fifth on the ladder due to points differential.
On the flip side, a victory for the Dolphins over one of the NRL heavyweights could hold them in good stead heading into their maiden finals campaign.
“They’re a big chance and if you get them in the semis and they catch fire, no one is beating them,” Johns said.
“If they beat the Roosters, I say they are a genuine chance.”
Johns believes the strike power in the Dolphins’ backline, led by the likes of Herbie Farnworth and Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow , could cause issues for the Tricolours.
Herbie Farnworth has cemented himself as the NRL’s best centre. Getty Images
He also pointed to the defensive issues on both of the Roosters’ edges as an area the Dolphins could look to expose, while labelling the absence of Victor Radley as a “really big out” after he was concussed against the Tigers.
The highly-anticipated match between the Roosters and Dolphins kicks off at 5.30pm on Saturday evening at Allianz Stadium.
